links.outcome: LLM vs junior and senior radiologists diagnostic performance (AUC) on BI-RADS 4 malignancy prediction
links.effect: LLM AUCs 0.61-0.64 vs junior 0.72 and senior 0.75; all three LLMs significantly worse than both radiologist groups (all P<.05); accuracy 60.8-63.5% vs 72.0-74.5%.
links.quote: DeLong testing confirmed that all three LLMs performed significantly worse than both junior and senior radiologists (all P<.05), and no significant difference was observed between the two radiologist groups (P=.55).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM predictions across repeated runs (Fleiss kappa)
links.effect: Fleiss kappa 0.850 for ChatGPT-4o, 0.824 for DeepSeek-R1, 0.732 for Claude 3 Opus.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated higher reproducibility than DeepSeek-R1 and Claude 3 Opus (Fleiss κ 0.850 vs 0.824 and 0.732, respectively).

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and reproducibility of several commercial LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus, DeepSeek-R1) in predicting malignancy from mammography report text compared to radiologists, but does not test a deployment practice or safeguard.
